extraction.name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
extraction.description: A large unified database of human motion that combines 15 optical marker-based mocap datasets into a common SMPL-based representation including pose, shape, and soft-tissue motion.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood; Nima Ghorbani; Nikolaus F. Troje; Gerard Pons-Moll; Michael J. Black
extraction.rai:dataCollection: AMASS was created by aggregating 15 motion capture datasets and converting their marker-based mocap data into a common SMPL representation using MoSh++; some datasets were downloaded publicly, some obtained privately, and some recorded by the authors.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper discusses missing markers due to occlusion during mocap sessions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data are optical marker-based motion capture recordings from 15 source datasets, with varying marker sets, and for SSM also synchronized 4D scans.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors mapped marker data into common SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters using MoSh++, and manually inspected results to correct or hold out problematic sequences with swapped or mislabeled markers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Marker-based mocap data were converted into SMPL body model parameters using MoSh++, producing per-frame shape, pose, and soft-tissue coefficients.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors manually inspected outputs and corrected or excluded problematic cases caused by swapped or mislabeled markers.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will continue to be expanded with new mocap data contributed by the authors and the community.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The source datasets are often narrowly focused on particular classes of motions, and existing mocap databases are limited in size and complexity.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes inherent mocap problems such as swapped and mislabeled markers, missing markers due to occlusion, and that current runtime for MoSh++ is not real-time.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for machine learning applications in animation and computer vision, and for generating training data for deep learning.

description.evidence: To address this, we introduce AMASS, a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization.

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: During a mocap session, markers may get occluded by the body due to pose. If multiple markers of a particular body part are occluded simultaneously, the optimization may result in unreliable and implausible poses

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We unify a large corpus of archival marker-based optical human mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We used MoSh++ to map this large amount of marker data into our common SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters. Due to inherent problems with mocap, such as swapped and mislabeled markers, we manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: With MoSh++ it is easy to add more data and we will continue to expand the dataset. We will continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by us and the community.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: While there are many motion capture datasets available online for research purposes [8, 42, 27, 14, 38, 4, 41, 5, 22, 32], they are often narrowly focused on a particular class of motions. Even the largest ones are too limited in size and variety to support serious deep learning models.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Due to inherent problems with mocap, such as swapped and mislabeled markers, we manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems. During a mocap session, markers may get occluded by the body due to pose. Current runtime for MoSh++ is not real-time.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: This paper addresses two interrelated goals. First, we develop a method to accurately recover the shape and pose of a person in motion from standard motion capture (mocap) marker data. This enables the second goal, which is to create the largest publicly available database of human motions that can enable machine learning for applications in animation and computer vision. The consistent representation of AMASS makes it readily useful for animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning.
